fields.meta_description: Build an intake form that collects client details and files online, then routes each new client by the service they ask for. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Intake Form That Sorts Every New Client
fields.hero_description: Build an intake form that hides the questions a client does not need and saves each answer and file to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Good Intake Form Does
fields.features_subheading: Each one removes a follow-up email you would otherwise send before the first meeting.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the answers

Hide each section until an earlier answer calls for it. A client with no dependents never sees that page, and a renter skips the questions written only for homeowners.
fields.feature_2:
Uploads beside the questions

Ask for each document on the screen where its question sits, such as a photo ID or pictures of the job. Every file is saved to that client's record with the date it arrived.
fields.feature_3:
One row per client

Save every submitted intake as a row in a database you own, with the answers and files attached. Search past clients by name, or export the whole table when the year closes out.
fields.feature_4:
Routing by answer

Send each new client to the person who handles that kind of work. A service type or a budget decides who gets the email or Slack alert, and who books the first meeting.
fields.feature_5:
Signatures before the first meeting

Put the engagement letter or the cancellation policy at the end of the intake and collect a typed or drawn signature. Each signed copy is stored next to its answers.
fields.feature_6:
The source code is yours

Export the full code of the intake form and its database to GitHub on paid plans. A developer can host it on your own servers or connect it to the client portal you already run.

fields.usecase_heading: Intake Forms for Firms and In-House Teams
fields.tab_content_1:
Last year's return arrives with the new client's answers

Halvorsen Tax Studio sends one link to every new client. Single filers never see the dependents page, and the rental income section opens only for clients who own a rental. Last year's return and this year's W-2s upload on the same screen. Anyone reporting rental income goes to Marta Lind, the senior preparer.
fields.tab_content_2:
A conflict check runs before anyone books a consultation

Pryor Lane Family Law asks each prospective client for their own name and their spouse's, including former names. The intake checks every name against past clients and opposing parties. A match holds the intake for Ruth Okafor, the conflicts partner. The booking calendar stays closed until she clears it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Rush requests go to the marketing lead first

Anyone at Northwind who needs a launch video or an event booth fills in one request form with the goal and the due date. Anything due in under 10 business days is marked as a rush and goes to Priya Shah, the marketing lead, in Slack. Every other request joins the Asana queue with its brief attached.
fields.tab_content_4:
Photos of the room come in with the budget

Homeowners start on a phone: pick the room, describe the job and add up to six photos. Jobs budgeted over $25,000 go to Sam Delgado, the owner of Birchwood Remodeling, who calls to arrange a site visit. Smaller jobs get a link to book an estimator, and each request is saved with its photos.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Work through these seven steps to decide what your intake form asks and who receives each answer, then build it in Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what the first meeting needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the facts and documents you need before you meet a new client: the service they want and anything you would otherwise ask on the call. Cut every question whose answer nobody reads before that first meeting.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put contact details first and leave signatures for the last screen. Keep each section to one screen on a phone. Read every question aloud once and rewrite any that a new client would have to ask you about.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Note which answers change the form. Rental income opens a rental section, and a client under 18 opens a section for a parent or guardian. Everyone else moves straight past both, and the form stays as short as their situation allows.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name the person for each kind of client, plus a fallback for anything that matches no rule. Decide whether that person hears about it by email or in Slack, and write down what counts as urgent enough to flag on arrival.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your sections and rules into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the intake form and the database table behind it. Change any question or rule later by prompting again, and the live form updates.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add the agreement at the end
fields.howto_step_6_des: Place any policy the client must accept, such as a cancellation fee or an engagement letter, after the last question. Add a signature field below it. Have a lawyer read any term you expect to enforce before real clients sign it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send a test client through it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form on a phone as a made-up client who triggers every rule. Check that the alert arrives and the uploaded files open. Then send the real link at the moment a client books, while there is still time to read the answers.
